subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw keep default steering as boundary-based behavior, or add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context?
rationale: This choice affects shared runtime semantics, channel UX, Codex/native runtime integration, and compatibility with existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt modes.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document the current model-boundary steering behavior as the supported default and handle only narrower admission bugs in separate issues.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with explicit backend rejection and fallback behavior.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle only after maintainer-approved upgrade proof across channels and runtimes.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with explicit backend rejection and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue and replacement PR history point to this person as the strongest owner for shared active-run steering and queue behavior.
